# Vibrato v0.1.0 (pre-release)

**Pre-release: tested by unit tests and short in-game sessions only.** The human camera, key layer and recorder have been run in game for a few minutes at a time. This exact jar has not been run in game. Expect rough edges.

Built from commit `b97deb3624b0424bd754f401e7151ebf5dd8b2de` (origin/master). Unit tests: 563 run, 0 failed.

## What Vibrato is

Vibrato is a Minecraft mod for Fabric that runs autonomous bots. It is a continuation of
[AltoClef](https://github.com/gaucho-matrero/altoclef) and uses [Baritone](https://github.com/cabaletta/baritone)
for pathfinding. See [FEATURES.md](https://github.com/DanielDavis05/Vibrato/blob/master/FEATURES.md) for the feature list.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 1.21.1
- Java 21 or newer
- Fabric Loader 0.16.0 or newer (the range declared in `fabric.mod.json`)
- Fabric API 0.116.7+1.21.1 or another 1.21.1 build

## Install

1. Place `vibrato-0.1.0.jar` in your `mods/` folder.
2. Baritone is bundled inside the jar. Do not install a separate Baritone jar.

For commands and settings, see [usage.md](https://github.com/DanielDavis05/Vibrato/blob/master/usage.md).
Type `@help` in chat for a quick guide. Vibrato commands start with `@`. Baritone commands start with `#`.

## What is new in this release

- **Human-like camera.** Camera movement uses submovements and overshoot. It is controlled by the `humanLook` switch.
- **Human-like key layer.** Baritone's movement keys are reshaped before they reach the game: hesitation, strafe taps,
  jump timing, a short forward release before drops of two or more blocks, and sprint-hops on straight flat sprints.
  Controlled by `humanKeys` and `humanHops`.
- **Behavioural humanization.** Search pauses, opportunistic pickup and idle glances. Controlled by `humanBehavior`.
- **Motion recorder.** `@record start <name> [human|bot]` and `@record stop` write a JSON Lines trace to
  `run/traces/<name>-<source>.jsonl`. Each file has a header line, then `mouse`, `key` and `tick` events.
- **Fitting and comparison scripts** in `scripts/human/` (`fit.py`, `discriminate.py`). These are developer tools.
- **Crafting loop guard.** Task chains now reject a task that re-enters itself or nests past 128 levels, and log a warning
  instead of recursing until a `StackOverflowError`. Stick collection from dead bushes now asks for sticks directly and no longer tries to make an axe from the sticks it is collecting, which was the loop seen in game.

## Known issues

- The bot can stall in open water. It can stand still for several seconds while a path is active. The cause is not yet confirmed.
- The crafting recursion guard is in this release and covered by unit tests. It has not been confirmed in game.
- The human layers (camera, key layer, behavioural humanization) are not validated in extended play. Their effect on
  movement quality is unmeasured.
- Speed and stop-and-go on the bundled test route are not yet at human levels.

## Kill switches

Set these as JVM arguments (`-D...`). Each one turns off one layer and leaves the rest of the bot running.

| Switch | Effect |
|---|---|
| `-Dvibrato.human=off` | Turns off all human layers (camera, keys, hops, behaviour). |
| `-Dvibrato.humanLook=off` | Turns off the human camera. |
| `-Dvibrato.humanKeys=off` | Turns off the human key layer. |
| `-Dvibrato.humanHops=off` | Turns off sprint-hops. |
| `-Dvibrato.humanBehavior=off` | Turns off search pauses, opportunistic pickup and idle glances. |
| `-Dvibrato.nav=off` | Turns off the navigation safety layer. |
